resources.string: ⚠️ Sidepeek can’t post notifications right now, so LINE’s own notifications are kept and no message is missed.\nTo have LINE notifications organized by chat, allow Sidepeek to show notifications and turn on its “LINE message preview” notification category.
The side panel isn’t set up yet. Notification organizing already works; come back and turn on the side panel when you have time.
Why turn on the side panel service?
① Try turning on the side panel service
Try ① first; do ② only if it’s blocked

Go to Accessibility → Installed apps → Sidepeek side panel and try to turn it on. If “App was denied access” appears, tap Close; only then does ⋮ → Allow restricted settings appear at the top right of App info. Then go back to Accessibility and turn the service on. The service only tells the home screen and keyboard apart and doesn’t read the screen by default.
Advanced: only if the side panel service can’t be turned on
Only if the system won’t let you turn on the side panel service. The downside is an extra persistent notification.
Three steps: notifications become conversations, a Peek bar sits at the screen edge, swipe in from it to open the side panel

A pile of LINE notifications becomes one conversation preview. A translucent “Peek bar” sits at the edge of the screen; swipe in from it to open the side panel (much like Samsung’s Edge panel handle).
Tap the button below and turn on “Sidepeek” in the list.
Optional, but without these you may miss messages or get the same message twice.
Tap an item to adjust it. Changes apply right away.
When collapsed, the system usually shows only the latest one or two; this number applies when expanded.
Side panel cards use the same spacing. More spacing means fewer messages fit in one notification.
The system draws it in one color; cut-out or simple shapes work best.

This is the small icon in the top row of the screen and on notifications. After choosing “Custom”, tap it again to change the picture. The small app icon at the bottom right of a notification is set by the system and can’t be changed.
Use one of the phone’s notification sounds or your own mp3. For vibration, pick a pattern or record your own rhythm.
Only changes the LINE notifications Sidepeek organizes. After changing, notifications briefly disappear and come back; no messages are lost.
When a group has no photo, its notification shows the first letter of its name. You can give each group your own picture; pictures stay on this phone.
Once you’ve read messages, Sidepeek clears their notifications. The messages stay in the side panel.

When on, reads the chat name at the top of LINE’s screen and matches it with the notifications. Chat content isn’t read or stored. If nothing matches, nothing is cleared, and you can swipe the notification away yourself.

⚠️ The accessibility service is off, so opening LINE directly won’t clear chat notifications\nOnly a chat you open from a Sidepeek notification is cleared. Turn on “Sidepeek side panel” in Accessibility settings to fix this.
Messages from the apps turned on here go into the side panel.

Tap “Choose other apps” to add any app on your phone. Only LINE notifications are reorganized; other apps stay as they are. Calls, download progress, music players and similar notifications are never collected.
Swipe past the dashed line to open; tap the picture to see it again. Hold the Peek bar for half a second, then drag up or down to move it.
Shown only in portrait; it hides automatically in landscape.
When does the Peek bar appear?
Besides swiping in from the Peek bar, there are three more ways. Tap a step to see it.
Add “Open message side panel” to Quick Settings

When editing the “Apps” Edge panel on a Samsung phone, you can add the “Open side panel” shortcut too.\n\nWhen opened from a home screen or Edge panel shortcut, Samsung switches the background back to the home screen. To stay where you are, use Quick Settings.
At most once a day; a notice appears at the top when there’s a new version.
When you open Sidepeek, it asks GitHub whether there’s a new version. It’s an ordinary web request that contains none of your data.
Notifications sound twice, or vibrate as one long buzz?

If the same LINE message rings or pops up twice, or the vibration becomes one long buzz, go to LINE’s App info → Notifications → Notification categories, tap the words “Message notifications” and choose Silent. If this doesn’t happen to you, leave it as is.

• Keep “Allow notifications” inside it on, or Sidepeek won’t receive messages.
• Don’t touch the incoming call and call categories, and don’t turn off the “Sound and vibration” switch on the previous page, or LINE calls may not pop up.
• LINE’s missed calls are also in “Message notifications”, but Sidepeek posts them, so they still ring after you set it to Silent.
Notifications stop popping up for a while?

If you swipe a pop-up notification up, new messages don’t pop up for about 60 seconds. This is Android’s own behavior: the system stops pop-ups from the same app for about 60 seconds. All LINE chats are posted by Sidepeek, so no chat pops up during that time, and the app can’t turn this off.\n\nNo messages are lost; they still arrive in the notification shade and the side panel. To avoid it, let the notification collapse by itself, or swipe it away sideways.

• Only “You have a new message”: in LINE → Settings → Notifications, turn on “Show message previews”. When it’s off, the notification has no text and Sidepeek can’t get it either.\n• Pop-up notifications show only one line: on a Samsung phone, go to Settings → Notifications → Notification pop-up style and choose “Detailed”; then in Settings → Apps → Sidepeek → Notifications, set “LINE message preview” to Alert and allow pop-ups.\n• Stickers missing: stickers need the internet to download; a placeholder shows until then.
Opening the side panel by accident, or triggering the back gesture?

Both are under “Peek bar style” in the Settings tab:
• Opening the panel by accident: lower the “Sensitivity” so you have to swipe further.
• Swiping in goes back instead: set “Distance from edge” to 12 dp or more, so the Peek bar moves out of the system’s back-gesture area.

The close-up picture shows the back-gesture area and the dashed line to swipe past, so you can compare while adjusting.
How should LINE’s notifications be set?

Sidepeek gets messages from LINE’s notifications, so LINE’s notifications must stay on:
• Phone Settings → Apps → LINE → Notifications: “Allow notifications” and “Sound and vibration” must be on; “Lock screen” and “Pop-up notifications” are recommended.
• LINE → Settings → Notifications: “Show message previews” must be on, or notifications have no text.
• Don’t touch the incoming call, in-call and call action categories, or LINE calls may not pop up.
• “Message notifications” can be set to Silent (see “Notifications sound twice, or vibrate as one long buzz?”), but keep “Allow notifications” inside it on.

A ringing LINE call is always shown by LINE itself. Missed calls are posted by Sidepeek: every one alerts you and also goes into the side panel.
Samsung’s Edge panel handle and Sidepeek’s Peek bar are separate and can be placed apart
Why turn on accessibility (the side panel service)?

It’s the recommended way to show the Peek bar at the screen edge, with no persistent notification. It’s also required to clear chat notifications when you open LINE directly. The system has it off by default, so turn it on once:
1. Try turning on “Sidepeek side panel” in Accessibility
2. If it’s blocked, tap Close, then in App info tap ⋮ at the top right → “Allow restricted settings”
3. Go back to Accessibility and turn it on again

The service doesn’t read the screen by default; only if you also turn on “Advanced clearing” does it read the chat name at the top of LINE’s screen. “Display over other apps” is only a fallback.
When does the Peek bar appear, and when does it hide?

• In other apps: by default it shows in every app, just like Samsung’s Edge panel handle. To show it only on the home screen, turn on “Show only on home screen”.
• While typing: it fades out while the keyboard is open so it never covers the keyboard or gets touched by mistake, and fades back in afterwards. Turn off “Hide while typing” if you don’t want this.
• Lock screen: hidden by default. With “Show on lock screen” on, swiping in asks you to unlock first, and no message content appears on the lock screen. Some system versions block it; if you can’t see it, turn the side panel service off and on again.
• Landscape: shown only in portrait; it hides automatically in landscape.

All these switches are under “When the Peek bar shows” in the Settings tab.
How is it related to Samsung’s Edge panels?

They are two separate things:
• Samsung Edge panels: system and app shortcuts, pulled out from the Edge panel handle
• Sidepeek side panel: messages from LINE, Instagram, Threads and other apps you choose, pulled out from the Peek bar

Samsung doesn’t let other apps add to its Edge panels, so the two can’t be merged. The handle and the Peek bar can sit on different sides or at different heights; if they overlap, move it under “Peek bar style” in the Settings tab.

You can also add the “Open side panel” shortcut to the Edge panel; see “Other ways to open the side panel” in the Settings tab.
Why does notification organizing only cover LINE?

LINE’s own notifications show only the latest message per chat, so earlier ones can’t be seen.

So Sidepeek takes over LINE: it posts a new notification for each chat listing every unread message, then hides LINE’s original notification.

Messenger, Instagram, Threads and Teams already show several messages from the same conversation, so they stay as they are and only go into the side panel. Choose which apps under “Apps to collect” in the Settings tab; any app on your phone can be added.

Tap “Email the developer” and describe what happened; your phone model and similar details are attached automatically. If the developer needs details, tap “Start full log”, let the app receive a few messages (ideally with stickers or photos), then tap “Export diagnostic log” and send the file to the developer.
